places.name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral, Kohima
places.summary: Kohima's hilltop cathedral of 1991, with one of Asia's largest carved wooden crosses; open 8 am–5 pm.
places.seoDescription: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral, Kohima: consecrated 1991, seats 3,000, with a 16-ft carved wooden crucifix. Open 8 am–5 pm.

images.commons: File:Mary Help of Christians Cathedral Kohima.jpg
images.alt: The tall, peaked front of Kohima's Mary Help of Christians Cathedral
images.caption: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral, Kohima

overview.text:
The Mary Help of Christians Cathedral stands on a hill in Kohima and is the main church of the city's Catholic diocese. Building began in 1986 and it was consecrated in 1991; its tall, sharply peaked front is one of the landmarks of the Kohima skyline.

It is big — the building covers 25,000 sq ft, its semicircular gallery of pews seats up to 3,000 people, and the whole compound can hold 20,000. Inside, look for the 16-foot carved wooden crucifix, one of the largest crosses in Asia, and the sign asking visitors to remember all those who gave their lives for Nagaland. The cathedral is open from 8 am to 5 pm, and visitors can attend prayers between 8 am and 4 pm.

places.name: Diezephe Craft Village
places.summary: A craft village of 500 weavers and artisans 13 km from Dimapur; Best Tourism Village bronze, 2023.
places.seoDescription: A craft village of 500 weavers and artisans 13 km from Dimapur; Best Tourism Village bronze, 2023.

overview.text: Diezephe, 13 km from Dimapur, is a craft village of some 500 artisans and weavers, where handloom and handicrafts are a way of life. Visitors can meet the makers directly and buy their work; the village won bronze as Best Tourism Village in 2023.

places.name: Liphanyan Governor's Camp
places.summary: A riverside camp on the Doyang, 45 km from Dimapur — picnics, camping, fishing and rafting.
places.seoDescription: A riverside camp on the Doyang, 45 km from Dimapur — picnics, camping, fishing and rafting.

overview.text: Liphanyan Governor's Camp lies about 45 km from Dimapur, in the forests of Wokha district beside the Doyang river. It is a quiet riverside spot for picnics, camping and fishing, and for rafting on the Doyang — an easy escape from the city.

places.name: Kohima Botanical Garden
places.summary: Medicinal plants, orchids and bamboos in the heart of Kohima; open 9 am–4 pm.
places.seoDescription: Medicinal plants, orchids and bamboos in the heart of Kohima; open 9 am–4 pm.

overview.text: Kohima Botanical Garden gathers medicinal plants, orchids and a wide range of bamboos in a green pocket of the city, including plants that grow only around Kohima. Allow two or three hours. It is open from 9 am to 4 pm.

places.name: Pulie Badze Wildlife Sanctuary
places.summary: A legendary forested peak near Kohima; 9.23 sq km sanctuary, open 6 am–5 pm.
places.seoDescription: A legendary forested peak near Kohima; 9.23 sq km sanctuary, open 6 am–5 pm.

overview.text: Pulie Badze is a forested peak near Kohima, wrapped in legend, and its wildlife sanctuary — set up in 1980 — protects about 9.23 sq km with more than 250 plant species. It is open from 6 am to 5 pm, and makes a good half-day walk from the capital.

places.name: Tuophema Village
places.summary: A welcoming village near Kohima — home-cooked meals and local crafts.
places.seoDescription: A welcoming village near Kohima — home-cooked meals and local crafts.

overview.text: Tuophema is a village in the foothills near Kohima where families welcome visitors, share their customs and cook home meals from local ingredients. Look for bamboo baskets, handwoven shawls and wood carvings made in the village — buying them supports the local economy.

places.name: Molungkimong Village
places.summary: A village 39 km from Mokokchung, where Nagaland's first church was founded in 1872.
places.seoDescription: A village 39 km from Mokokchung, where Nagaland's first church was founded in 1872.

overview.text: Molungkimong, about 39 km from Mokokchung, is a village believed to date from 1303. It holds a special place in Naga history: the first church in Nagaland was founded here on 22 December 1872. Villagers still make bamboo baskets, mats and woven crafts.
